gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-ovo: Ovo is a text serif whose thins barely lighten. Edo SZ's cast-iron stature, drawn in one constant stroke, is the pair's real draw, with no swelling where curves meet stems.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-ovo: Towering lowercase, strolling along with a relaxed, adventurous stride. Eight Bit Dragon supplies the bold show, while Ovo, a text serif with spacious curve endings, settles into the paragraphs.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-halant: Electroharmonix breaks every word into lone, widely spaced letters. That commanding display does the shouting best, while Halant, with its faint stroke modulation and outward-pointing terminals, does the quiet reading.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-scope-one: Existence has counters like wide glass portholes and letter parts of matching visual mass. Scope One, a text serif with stubby ascenders and counters that spill outward, fills the page more softly.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-hanuman: Tall, tightly packed letters give Franchise a strong, clean stance, with c tips pulled well apart. And Hanuman, with its high-waisted lowercase, is worth giving a touch more size.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-pridi: Tall, jammed-together letters give Franchise a strong, clean look up top. Pridi, a text serif with proud, almost capital-sized lowercase and generous curve gaps, would carry a paragraph with an open, unhurried feel.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-scope-one: Scope One, a text serif whose counters spill outward beside stubby ascenders, sits beneath Franchise's tall, wire-like lines. Paragraphs set in it read in a relaxed, unhurried, generous way.
gen-dafont-franchise-switzer: Tight-packed and tall, Franchise looks strong and clean at a glance, its c tips pulled apart. But Switzer, a sans with tubular, wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line, is what ties the pair together.
gen-dafont-galaxy-gf-ovo: Cosmic, marker-like lines and loose, generous letterfit up top. Ovo, a text serif with only modest contrast, settles in below, so the constant heading line and the gentle body modulation play off each other.
gen-dafont-gobold-switzer: Switzer, a sans with tubular, wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line, sits quietly beneath Gobold's far-spread, commanding letters. Those curves that refuse to close are the memorable part.
